about.description:
Runtime dynamically-linked library only.

SystemC(TM) addresses the need for a system design and verification language that spans hardware
and software. It is a language built in standard C++ by extending the language with the use of
class libraries. The language is particularly suited to model system's partitioning, to evaluate
and verify the assignment of blocks to either hardware or software implementations, and to
architect and measure the interactions between and among functional blocks. Leading companies in
the intellectual property (IP), electronic design automation (EDA), semiconductor, electronic
systems, and embedded software industries currently use SystemC for architectural exploration,
to deliver high-performance hardware blocks at various levels of abstraction and to develop
virtual platforms for hardware/software co-design. SystemC has been standardized by the Open
SystemC Initiative (OSCI) and Accellera Systems Initiative and ratified as IEEE Std. 1666(TM)-2011.
about.summary: The language for System-level design, modeling and verification

raw_meta_yaml:
schema_version: 1

context:
  version: "3.0.2"
  major_minor: "3.0"

recipe:
  name: systemc-split
  version: ${{ version }}

source:
  url: https://github.com/accellera-official/systemc/archive/refs/tags/${{ version }}.tar.gz
  sha256: 9b3693ed286aab958b9e5d79bb0ad3bc523bbc46931100553275352038f4a0c4
  patches:
    - if: not win
      then: patches/0001-examples-sysc-2.3-simple_async-needs-PTHREADS.patch

build:
  number: 1

outputs:
  - package:
      name: libsystemc
    build:
      skip:
        - win
      script: build
      files:
        - if: linux
          then: lib/libsystemc.so.?.?.?
        - if: osx
          then: lib/libsystemc.?.?.?.dylib
    requirements:
      build:
        - if: unix
          then: gnuconfig
        - ${{ compiler("cxx") }}
        - ${{ stdlib("c") }}
        - if: not win
          then: make
        - if: not win
          then: autoconf
        - if: not win
          then: automake
        - if: not win
          then: libtool
        - cmake
      run_exports:
        - ${{ pin_subpackage("libsystemc", upper_bound="x.x.x") }}
    tests:
      - script:
          - if: linux
            then: test -f "$PREFIX"/lib/libsystemc"$SHLIB_EXT".${{ version }}
          - if: osx
            then: test -f "$PREFIX"/lib/libsystemc.${{ version }}"$SHLIB_EXT"
    about:
      description: |
        Runtime dynamically-linked library only.

        SystemC(TM) addresses the need for a system design and verification language that spans hardware
        and software. It is a language built in standard C++ by extending the language with the use of
        class libraries. The language is particularly suited to model system's partitioning, to evaluate
        and verify the assignment of blocks to either hardware or software implementations, and to
        architect and measure the interactions between and among functional blocks. Leading companies in
        the intellectual property (IP), electronic design automation (EDA), semiconductor, electronic
        systems, and embedded software industries currently use SystemC for architectural exploration,
        to deliver high-performance hardware blocks at various levels of abstraction and to develop
        virtual platforms for hardware/software co-design. SystemC has been standardized by the Open
        SystemC Initiative (OSCI) and Accellera Systems Initiative and ratified as IEEE Std. 1666(TM)-2011.

  - package:
      name: systemc-doc
    build:
      script: build
      files:
        - if: win
          then: Library/share/doc/systemc/
        - if: not win
          then: share/doc/systemc/
    requirements:
      build:
        - if: unix
          then: gnuconfig
        - ${{ compiler("cxx") }}
        - ${{ stdlib("c") }}
        - if: not win
          then: make
        - if: not win
          then: autoconf
        - if: not win
          then: automake
        - if: not win
          then: libtool
        - cmake
    about:
      description: |
        Documentation installed by upstream build into $PREFIX along with the examples.
        On Windows, the documentation is a bit light but the examples are in here.

        SystemC(TM) addresses the need for a system design and verification language that spans hardware
        and software. It is a language built in standard C++ by extending the language with the use of
        class libraries. The language is particularly suited to model system's partitioning, to evaluate
        and verify the assignment of blocks to either hardware or software implementations, and to
        architect and measure the interactions between and among functional blocks. Leading companies in
        the intellectual property (IP), electronic design automation (EDA), semiconductor, electronic
        systems, and embedded software industries currently use SystemC for architectural exploration,
        to deliver high-performance hardware blocks at various levels of abstraction and to develop
        virtual platforms for hardware/software co-design. SystemC has been standardized by the Open
        SystemC Initiative (OSCI) and Accellera Systems Initiative and ratified as IEEE Std. 1666(TM)-2011.

  - package:
      name: systemc-dev
    build:
      script: build
      files:
        - if: linux
          then: lib/libsystemc.so
        - if: linux
          then: lib/libsystemc.so.?.?
        - if: osx
          then: lib/libsystemc.dylib
        - if: osx
          then: lib/libsystemc.?.?.dylib
        - if: win
          then: Library/lib/systemc.lib
        - if: not win
          then: lib/pkgconfig/systemc.pc
        - if: not win
          then: lib/pkgconfig/tlm.pc
        - if: win
          then: Library/lib/cmake/SystemCLanguage/
        - if: win
          then: Library/lib/cmake/SystemCTLM/
        - if: win
          then: Library/include/sysc/
        - if: win
          then: Library/include/systemc*
        - if: win
          then: Library/include/tlm*
        - if: win
          then: Library/include/tlm_core/
        - if: win
          then: Library/include/tlm_utils/
        - if: not win
          then: lib/cmake/SystemCLanguage/
        - if: not win
          then: lib/cmake/SystemCTLM/
        - if: not win
          then: include/sysc/
        - if: not win
          then: include/systemc*
        - if: not win
          then: include/tlm*
        - if: not win
          then: include/tlm_core/
        - if: not win
          then: include/tlm_utils/
        - if: not win
          then: etc/conda/*activate.d/*activate-systemc-dev.sh
    requirements:
      build:
        - if: unix
          then: gnuconfig
        - ${{ compiler("cxx") }}
        - ${{ stdlib("c") }}
        - if: not win
          then: make
        - if: not win
          then: autoconf
        - if: not win
          then: automake
        - if: not win
          then: libtool
        - cmake
      host:
        - ${{ pin_subpackage("systemc-doc", exact=True) }}
      run:
        - if: not win
          then: ${{ pin_subpackage("libsystemc", exact=True) }}
      run_exports:
        - if: not win
          then: ${{ pin_subpackage("libsystemc", upper_bound="x.x.x") }}
    tests:
      - script:
          - if: win
            then: echo on
          - if: win
            then: xcopy %LIBRARY_PREFIX%\share\doc\systemc\examples examples\ /F /E /H
          - if: win
            then: cd examples\build-msvc
          - if: win and target_platform == "win-64"
            then: nmake /nologo CONFIG=Release PLATFORM=x64 VCBUILD=vcbuild check
          - if: not win
            then: test "$SYSTEMC_HOME" == "$PREFIX"
          - if: not win
            then: ls -l "$PREFIX"/lib
          - if: not win
            then: test -f "$PREFIX"/lib/libsystemc"$SHLIB_EXT"
          - if: linux
            then: test -f "$PREFIX"/lib/libsystemc"$SHLIB_EXT".${{ major_minor }}
          - if: osx
            then: test -f "$PREFIX"/lib/libsystemc.${{ major_minor }}"$SHLIB_EXT"
          - if: not win
            then: pkg-config --print-provides systemc
          - if: not win
            then: pkg-config --print-errors --exact-version=$PKG_VERSION systemc
          - if: not win
            then: pkg-config --print-provides tlm
          - if: not win
            then: cp -r "$PREFIX"/share/doc/systemc/examples .
          - if: not win
            then: "sed -i 's|$(EXE): $(OBJS) $(SYSTEMC_LIB_DIR)/libsystemc.a|$(EXE): $(OBJS)|' examples/build-unix/Makefile.rules"
          - if: linux
            then: make -C examples/build-unix -j $CPU_COUNT run
          - if: linux
            then: make -C examples/build-unix -j $CPU_COUNT check
          - if: osx
            then: make -C examples/build-unix -j $CPU_COUNT run LDFLAG_RPATH=-Wl,-rpath, FLAGS_WERROR="-Werror -Wno-error=invalid-utf8"
          - if: osx
            then: make -C examples/build-unix -j $CPU_COUNT check LDFLAG_RPATH=-Wl,-rpath, FLAGS_WERROR="-Werror -Wno-error=invalid-utf8"
        requirements:
          build:
            - ${{ compiler("cxx") }}
          run:
            - ${{ pin_subpackage("systemc-doc", exact=True) }}
            - if: not win
              then: make
            - if: not win
              then: sed
            - if: not win
              then: pkg-config
    about:
      description: |
        Everything needed for development using System-C. Headers, unversioned dyn-lib symlinks (unix)
        and the static systemc.lib (Windows).

        SystemC(TM) addresses the need for a system design and verification language that spans hardware
        and software. It is a language built in standard C++ by extending the language with the use of
        class libraries. The language is particularly suited to model system's partitioning, to evaluate
        and verify the assignment of blocks to either hardware or software implementations, and to
        architect and measure the interactions between and among functional blocks. Leading companies in
        the intellectual property (IP), electronic design automation (EDA), semiconductor, electronic
        systems, and embedded software industries currently use SystemC for architectural exploration,
        to deliver high-performance hardware blocks at various levels of abstraction and to develop
        virtual platforms for hardware/software co-design. SystemC has been standardized by the Open
        SystemC Initiative (OSCI) and Accellera Systems Initiative and ratified as IEEE Std. 1666(TM)-2011.

  - package:
      name: systemc
    requirements:
      run:
        - ${{ pin_subpackage("systemc-dev", exact=True) }}
        - ${{ pin_subpackage("systemc-doc", exact=True) }}
      run_exports:
        - if: not win
          then: ${{ pin_subpackage("libsystemc", upper_bound="x.x.x") }}
    about:
      description: |
        Metapackage containing everything for development and runtime.

        SystemC(TM) addresses the need for a system design and verification language that spans hardware
        and software. It is a language built in standard C++ by extending the language with the use of
        class libraries. The language is particularly suited to model system's partitioning, to evaluate
        and verify the assignment of blocks to either hardware or software implementations, and to
        architect and measure the interactions between and among functional blocks. Leading companies in
        the intellectual property (IP), electronic design automation (EDA), semiconductor, electronic
        systems, and embedded software industries currently use SystemC for architectural exploration,
        to deliver high-performance hardware blocks at various levels of abstraction and to develop
        virtual platforms for hardware/software co-design. SystemC has been standardized by the Open
        SystemC Initiative (OSCI) and Accellera Systems Initiative and ratified as IEEE Std. 1666(TM)-2011.
